item.title: Datroway (AstraZeneca/Daiichi Sankyo)
item.description:
• Summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted approval to AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Datroway (datopotamab deruxtecan) for the first-line treatment of triple-negative breast cancer, outpacing Gilead's Trodelvy. The decision was based on the TROPION-Breast02 trial, which demonstrated statistically significant improvements in progression-free survival and overall survival. Datroway is a TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate that delivers a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, offering a new option for patients with this aggressive subtype.
  • MoAs: TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) with topoisomerase I inhibitor (DXd) payload
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma, Endpoints News

item.title: AstraZeneca Breast Cancer Drug (EU vs FDA)
item.description:
• Summary: Regulatory opinions diverged sharply for AstraZeneca's breast cancer drug Datroway (datopotamab deruxtecan). The European Medicines Agency's CHMP issued a positive opinion supporting approval for use in advanced breast cancer, citing robust efficacy data. In contrast, a U.S. FDA advisory committee voted against the drug earlier this year, raising concerns about interstitial lung disease and other toxicities. The split underscores differing benefit–risk assessments across regions, with the EU prioritizing the drug's clinical benefit in a population with limited options.
  • MoAs: TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) with topoisomerase I inhibitor (DXd) payload
  • Sources: Endpoints News, Fierce Pharma, STAT News

item.title: Merck/Kelun TROP2 ADC in Lung Cancer
item.description:
• Summary: Merck and Kelun-Biotech reported positive Phase 3 data for their TROP2-directed ADC SKB264 (MK-2870) in first-line non-small cell lung cancer. When combined with Keytruda (pembrolizumab), the ADC significantly improved overall survival versus chemotherapy plus Keytruda alone. The results validate the TROP2–Keytruda pairing as a potential new standard of care. The data also highlight the growing competitiveness of the ADC landscape, with multiple players pursuing TROP2 targets.
  • MoAs: TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) with topoisomerase I inhibitor payload
  • Sources: BioSpace, ApexOnco, Fierce Pharma

item.title: Ovarian Cancer (OSE Immunotherapeutics)
item.description:
• Summary: OSE Immunotherapeutics reported a Phase 2 clinical trial win in ovarian cancer, supported by combination with Keytruda (pembrolizumab). The positive data marks a significant step for the company in this indication.
  • MoAs: pembrolizumab: anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor; OSE Immunotherapeutics' investigational agent: mechanism not specified in available information.
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech
